classifiedFindings.evidence: The generic counting screen turns distinct approved tasks into the same tappable grid: m3-math-02-a2 loses the adult's model; m3-math-05-a1 loses the line; m3-math-06-a2 collapses mine/yours; m3-math-07-a2 loses the circle; m3-math-11-a2 cannot split five objects into two piles; m3-math-12-a2 reveals the hidden complement; m3-math-13-a1 collapses two real collections; m3-math-14-a2 loses the model pile; and m3-math-15-a2 loses the number strip and finger representation. Additional examples: m3-math-16-a1 replaces hide-and-guess on the number strip with counting ten dots, and m3-math-17-a2 replaces showing and hiding fingers with the same count-to-ten grid. Further examples: m3-math-20-a2 omits the original collection that must be rebuilt, and m3-math-21-a2 omits the separate piles and number strip required by the task.
classifiedFindings.scope: Counting renderer and approved activity semantics; requires a bounded pedagogical decision before changing layout, data or success behavior.

classifiedFindings.evidence: m3-math-03-a2 labels four bins by shape, accepts visibly mismatched placements, states there is no wrong answer, then says « Tout est rangé. Bravo ! » when every token has merely been placed.
classifiedFindings.scope: GroupAndMatch feedback contract and approved sorting pedagogy; decide between open unlabelled sorting and checked labelled groups before implementation.

classifiedFindings.evidence: m3-math-08-a1 asks the child to find the shape matching « celle-ci », and its approved guidance requires comparing differently sized/oriented pairs, but the child screen shows no model shape and instead asks « Montre : carré ».
classifiedFindings.scope: Matching renderer and approved comparison semantics; provide an explicit model/pair interaction without altering the approved instruction.

classifiedFindings.evidence: m3-math-08-a2 asks the child to find and name a shape in the room, but the child screen requires selecting a predetermined on-screen square and grades that tap. The same conversion appears in m3-world-05-a1, where comparing two animals becomes choosing « poule », and m3-math-18-a1, where matching a paper shape to a real object face becomes choosing « carré ».
classifiedFindings.scope: Observation and matching renderer semantics; preserve approved real-world tasks and avoid inventing fixed on-screen answers.

classifiedFindings.evidence: m3-math-10-a1 is « De dix à vingt », but the child counter starts at 1, passes through 10 without a transition and finishes at 20, changing the practiced sequence to 1–20.

classifiedFindings.evidence: m3-lang-13-a2 teaches five market words, but only four media assets are linked; « la monnaie » renders as an empty picture card.
classifiedFindings.scope: Vocabulary/media pairing and word-card fallback; preserve the approved five-word instruction and supply an intentional representation for every taught word.

classifiedFindings.evidence: m3-math-18-a2 asks for a house made from a square wall and triangle roof, but its look-only panel shows four isolated shapes, including a rectangle and circle, with no house composition.

classifiedFindings.evidence: m3-math-19-a1 is titled « De un à trente » and has upTo 30, but the rendered interaction contains twenty targets and ends with « 20 en tout. Bravo ! ».

classifiedFindings.evidence: m1-time-15-a1 and m1-world-16-a1 intentionally have no media because the child must observe the real environment, but the look-and-name renderer shows only « À observer » and never supplies the existing « Posez l’écran » handoff.

Use grammatical generic choice and retry copy for both shapes and vocabulary.
Remove false empty-picture stages from intentionally text-only vocabulary.
